Long tail, many mitochondria, packed with enzymes

walkthroughs.body_html:
Cells are shaped for their job. This is called specialisation.

- Sperm: tail to swim, lots of mitochondria for energy, acrosome enzymes to break into egg.
- Red blood cell: no nucleus (more room), biconcave shape, packed with haemoglobin.
- Nerve cell: long axon, branches at ends to connect.
- Muscle cell: long, lots of mitochondria, contains protein fibres.
- Root hair cell: long projection → huge surface area for absorbing water.

Stem cells are unspecialised — they can divide and turn into other cell types.

- Embryonic stem cells can become any cell type. Powerful, but using embryos raises ethical concerns.
- Adult stem cells (e.g. bone marrow) can only become a few types — used to treat leukaemia.
- Plant stem cells in meristems can clone whole plants.

Risks: rejection, viral infection from donor cells.

One cell becomes two in three big stages:

1. Interphase — cell grows, copies its DNA and organelles.
2. Mitosis — chromosomes line up and are pulled apart into two identical nuclei.
3. Cytokinesis — cytoplasm and membrane split into two daughter cells.

Result: two cells genetically identical to the parent.

mcqs.q: Why does a sperm cell have many mitochondria?
options: To carry oxygen
To release energy for swimming
To digest the egg
To copy its DNA

mcqs.q: Which stem cell can become ANY cell type in the body?
options: Adult bone marrow
Embryonic
Plant root cell
Red blood cell

mcqs.q: What is the key structural difference between prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells?
options: Prokaryotes have no DNA — that's why they have no nucleus.
Eukaryotes have a membrane-bound nucleus and membrane-bound organelles; prokaryotes do not.
Mitosis happens in plants and meiosis happens in animals.
Prokaryotes are always smaller than 1 micrometre and have no cytoplasm.

mcqs.q: What is the key difference between mitosis and meiosis?
options: Prokaryotes are always smaller than 1 micrometre and have no cytoplasm.
Mitosis produces two genetically identical diploid cells; meiosis produces four genetically different haploid cells (gametes).
Mitosis happens in plants and meiosis happens in animals.
Mitosis and meiosis both produce gametes; they are basically the same.
Stem cells are simply cells that haven't grown big enough yet.
An undifferentiated cell capable of dividing to produce more stem cells or differentiating into specialised cell types.
Prokaryotes are always smaller than 1 micrometre and have no cytoplasm.
Stem cells are taken only from embryos and cannot be found in adults.
